sources.citation: OLAC (Open Language Archives Community). Resources in and about the Ajawa language [ajw]. language-archives.org, combined catalog page as of 2024-12-18 (the Internet Archive snapshot 2024-12-19).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Catalog only. Four entries: 'Glottolog 5.1 Resources for Ajawa' (language descriptions category, i.e. the Glottolog record itself), 'Ajawa: a language of Nigeria' (Ethnologue 2018), 'LINGUIST List Resources for Ajawa' (2022), and 'A Sociolinguistic Profile of the West Chadic North Bauchi Languages of Bauchi and Jigawa States, Nigeria' (Gobak, Decker et al. 2022, SIL, oai:sil.org:94228). No primary texts, no lexical resources, no archive deposit anywhere in the OLAC network. Listed here so the bibliography row 'OLAC resources page for [ajw] -- not accessible' can be marked read.

During group interviews with the Burku, Choogen, and Gala, the people reported contact with the Ajawa. They confirmed that the language is no longer spoken, but the people maintain their identity.' sources.citation: Osaji, Bede. 1979. Language Survey in Nigeria. Publication B-81. Quebec: International Center for Research on Bilingualism (CIRB), Laval University. 180 pp. (ERIC document ED179113; microfiche digitized on archive.org, item micro_IA41155110_0593).
sources.note: Nothing. Ajawa is not in the main language inventory at all; it is relegated to Table 6 'Unidentifiable Nigerian language names' (names found in the literature that could not be verified as languages), entry 3: '1. Ajawa 2. Gunn 1953; Temple 1919; Nitecki 1972; Meek (Thomas) 1925; Greenberg 1963. 3. 545 in Bauchi Emirate; Darazo and Ganjuwa Districts, mainly in village of Kworko 4. ? dialect of Warji', plus the cross-reference 'Kworko -- Gunn 1953 -- See Ajawa'. Confirms from a 1970s Nigerian-languages inventory that no linguistic material on Ajawa was known.

sources.citation: Skinner, A. Neil. 1977. North Bauchi Chadic languages: common roots. Afroasiatic Linguistics 4(1): 1-49. Malibu: Undena.
sources.note: Nothing on Ajawa. p.3: 'There are two other languages in the group, of which one, Hausa Ajanci, is now reported to be extinct.' Ajanci was not elicited and is absent from the comparative wordlist; the phonetic-inventory section (p.5) covers the eight recorded languages only and says nothing about stress even for them.
